prompt: How many minutes did `Hierarchy.swift` report for the week?
Why did the mock exam's 60 minutes not count in `Hierarchy.swift`?

choices.text: `reduce` skips subclasses
choices.why: `reduce` added every element it was given.

choices.text: It inherited `StudyItem`'s `0`, and nobody overrode it
choices.why: Right: it sits under `Exam`, which never overrode `minutes` either.

choices.text: `length` was declared as a `let`
choices.why: A `let` is read normally; nothing reads `length` here.

choices.text: The array of `StudyItem` copied it without its own fields
choices.why: Class instances are not copied into an array; the object is whole.

prompt: Why does `MockExam` declare `length` again, when `StudySession` already has it?

choices.text: To override `StudySession`'s value
choices.why: `MockExam` is not a `StudySession`, so there is nothing to override.

choices.text: Swift requires every class to declare its stored properties twice
choices.why: No such rule exists.

choices.text: It has one superclass, `Exam`
choices.why: Right: what lives in `StudySession` has to be copied.

choices.text: Because `length` is private to `StudySession`
choices.why: It is not private; it is out of reach because of the tree.

prompt: The planner needs a "has a due date" property for some items. In the class tree, where does it end up?
hint: Every item in the array must answer it.

choices.text: In a protocol `Due`, conformed to only by the items that have one
choices.why: That is the composition answer, not the tree's.

choices.text: In `StudyItem`, answered by all
choices.why: Right: the base class grows, with a guessed default for everything without a due date.

choices.text: Only in `MockExam`
choices.why: Then the array of `StudyItem` could not ask the other items.

choices.text: In a second superclass of each class that needs it
choices.why: A class has one superclass.

prompt: In `Composed.swift`, what happens if you put an `Exam` into `timed: [any Timed]`?

choices.text: It counts as 0 minutes
choices.why: That was the tree's guess; here there is none.

choices.text: A compile error: `Exam` is not `Timed`
choices.why: Right: the wrong total becomes a refusal.

choices.text: A crash when the total is computed
choices.why: Conformance is checked before anything runs.

choices.text: The exam's grade is added instead

prompt: What total did `Composed.swift` print?
Which of these does `report(_ item: some Titled & Graded)` refuse?

choices.text: An `Exam`

choices.text: A `MockExam`
choices.why: A mock exam is all three, which includes both.

choices.text: A `StudySession`

choices.text: Any struct that conforms to `Titled`, whatever else it has

hint: Section 03 put the term in bold.

prompt: In `Mixins.swift`, where does `isLong` come from on a `StudySession`?

choices.text: From `extension Timed`
choices.why: Right: every timed type gets it.

choices.text: From the struct's own declaration
choices.why: The struct declares two stored properties and nothing else.

choices.text: From a base class called `Timed`
choices.why: `Timed` is a protocol, and there is no class here.

choices.text: From `Sequence`, through `totalMinutes`
choices.why: `totalMinutes` is on the week, not on one session.

prompt: Why does `Break(minutes: 40)` have no `label`?

choices.text: `label` is private
choices.why: It is not; the sessions use it.

choices.text: A break is shorter than 60 minutes
choices.why: The length decides `isLong`, not `label`.

choices.text: Mixins only work on the first type declared in a file
choices.why: Order in the file decides nothing.

choices.text: `label` exists only on types that are `Titled` and `Timed`
choices.why: Right: `Break` is timed and has no title.

prompt: What did `week.totalMinutes` print in `Mixins.swift`?
An extension of `Timed` starts needing `self.dueDate`, which `Timed` does not require. What does section 04 conclude?

choices.text: Cast `self` to the type that has it
choices.why: That ties a capability to one type and fails for the rest.

choices.text: A requirement is missing, or the member belongs to a type
choices.why: Right: either the capability needs it, or the extension is in the wrong place.

choices.text: Store `dueDate` in the extension
choices.why: Extensions add no storage.

choices.text: Mark the extension `final`
choices.why: `final` applies to classes and their members, and changes nothing here.

prompt: Why does `Reminder` hold an `any Clock` instead of calling `Date()` itself?

choices.text: `Date()` does not work on Linux
choices.why: `SystemClock` calls `Date()` on Linux and it works.

choices.text: A protocol is faster than a function call
choices.why: Speed is not the reason, and the box costs a lookup.

choices.text: So that a test passes in a clock it controls
choices.why: Right: the same code, with Monday fixed, gives the same answer every day.

choices.text: So that the reminder works in several time zones at once
choices.why: The seam is about who decides the time, not about time zones.

prompt: With `SystemClock`, `Reminder.swift` printed `system: []`. Why?

choices.text: The system clock is broken in the lab
choices.why: It gave the real date.

choices.text: `SystemClock` returns `nil` on Linux
choices.why: `now()` returns a `Date`, never `nil`.

choices.text: `filter` cannot compare `DateComponents`
choices.why: The fixed clock's line found two sessions with the same filter.

choices.text: It ran on 30 October 2026, and no session falls on that day
choices.why: Right: the answer depends on the day, which is the reason for the seam.

prompt: A teammate adds `var testDate: Date?` to `Reminder` and checks it before asking the system. What does section 05 say is wrong with that?

choices.text: The test lives inside the product
choices.why: Right: and each new dependency adds another flag.

choices.text: An optional `Date` does not compile in a struct
choices.why: It compiles; the objection is about design.

choices.text: Nothing: a flag and a protocol are the same seam
choices.why: The section argues the opposite.

choices.text: The reminder becomes slower to run in the app
choices.why: Speed is not the objection.

prompt: What does `final class Planner` prevent?

choices.text: Changing its `var` properties
choices.why: `final` is about subclassing, not mutation.

choices.text: Subclassing it
choices.why: Right: `inheritance from a final class 'Planner'` is refused.

choices.text: Creating more than one instance
choices.why: Any number of planners can be created.

choices.text: Conforming it to a protocol later in an extension
choices.why: Extensions and conformances still work on a final class.

prompt: Which of these are reasons section 06 gives for a class? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: One object shared on purpose, whose changes everyone sees
choices.why: Yes: identity.

choices.text: Something with a lifetime, closed when the last user lets go
choices.why: Yes: `deinit` exists only on classes.

choices.text: A type that is timed and graded
choices.why: That is two protocols, section 03.

choices.text: A framework that hands you a base class
choices.why: Yes: `UIViewController`, for one.

prompt: Why is `final` the cheap default for a new class?

choices.text: A final class uses less memory per instance
choices.why: The instance's size does not change.

choices.text: Swift adds `final` to every class anyway
choices.why: It does not; `SharedPlanner` would compile without it.

choices.text: Removing it later is easy; adding it after others subclass is not
choices.why: Right: the decision stays reversible in one direction only.

choices.text: Final classes are value types
choices.why: They are still classes, with identity.
